questions.q: What is aerobic respiration?
questions.a: Breakdown of glucose using oxygen to give CO2, water and much energy, inside mitochondria.

questions.q: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration.
questions.a: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy.

questions.q: Where in the cell does aerobic respiration occur?
questions.a: In the mitochondria - the cell's powerhouses.

questions.q: What is anaerobic respiration in yeast called and what does it give?
questions.a: Fermentation - glucose breaks down without oxygen into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Give one industrial use of yeast fermentation.
questions.a: Making bread (CO2 raises dough) and brewing alcohol.

questions.q: Why is less energy released in anaerobic respiration?
questions.a: Glucose is only partly broken down, so much energy stays locked in the products.

questions.q: Why do our muscles cramp after heavy exercise?
questions.a: Short of oxygen, muscles respire anaerobically making lactic acid, which causes cramps.

questions.q: What does muscle anaerobic respiration produce?
questions.a: Lactic acid (plus a little energy) from glucose without oxygen.

questions.q: How is the cramp relieved?
questions.a: Rest and a hot water bath improve blood flow, washing lactic acid away.

solution_steps.name: breaths_10min
solution_steps.explain: breaths in ten minutes at this rate

questions.q: A person takes 66 breaths in 3 minutes at rest. Find the breathing rate per minute and per hour.
questions.a: 1320 breaths/min

questions.q: After exercise a runner breathes 120 times in 2 minutes. Calculate the breathing rate.
questions.a: 3600 breaths/min

questions.q: A child breathes 100 times in 4 minutes. What is the rate per minute, and per hour?
questions.a: 1500 breaths/min

questions.q: During sleep 72 breaths occur in 3 minutes. Find the breathing rate.
questions.a: 1440 breaths/min

questions.q: A swimmer holds practice breathing of 90 breaths in 1.5 minutes. Compute the rate.
questions.a: 3600 breaths/min

questions.q: What happens when we breathe in?
questions.a: The diaphragm flattens and ribs rise; chest space grows, pressure falls and air rushes into the lungs.

questions.q: Which muscle plays the main role in breathing?
questions.a: The diaphragm, a sheet below the lungs that moves down and up.

questions.q: Why is the breathing rate faster during exercise?
questions.a: Muscles need more oxygen and must release more CO2, so breathing speeds up.

questions.q: A student's chest measures 30 inches after normal exhale and 33 inches after deep inhale. Find the chest expansion.
questions.a: 3 inches

questions.q: Chest reading is 28 inches exhaled and 31 inches inhaled. Calculate the expansion.
questions.a: 3 inches

questions.q: An athlete's chest goes from 34 to 38 inches between exhale and inhale. What is the expansion?
questions.a: 4 inches

questions.q: Measurements of 26 and 28.5 inches give what chest expansion?
questions.a: 2.5 inches

questions.q: A person exhales at 32 inches and inhales at 35.5 inches. Find the expansion.
questions.a: 3.5 inches

concepts.title: Composition of Inhaled and Exhaled Air

solution_steps.name: used_fraction
solution_steps.explain: fraction of oxygen the body used

questions.q: Inhaled air has 21% oxygen and exhaled air about 16%. What per cent of oxygen is consumed by the body?
If exhaled air holds 17% oxygen while inhaled has 21%, what percentage is used up?
A sample of exhaled air shows 15.5% oxygen. With inhaled at 21%, compute the consumption.
In an experiment inhaled oxygen is 20.9% and exhaled 16.4%. Find the oxygen taken by the body.
Fish-like efficiency aside, a diver's tank air has 21% O2 and exhaled bubbles show 18%. What was consumed?
How do insects breathe?
questions.a: Air enters through tiny holes (spiracles) into tubes called tracheae that reach every cell.

questions.q: What are spiracles?
questions.a: Small openings on an insect's body sides through which air enters the tracheal system.

questions.q: Why do insects not need lungs?
questions.a: Their tracheal tubes deliver air directly to cells, so blood need not carry oxygen.

questions.q: How do earthworms breathe?
questions.a: Oxygen dissolves on their moist skin and passes into blood capillaries beneath it.

questions.q: Why must earthworms stay in moist soil?
questions.a: Their skin must stay moist for oxygen to diffuse through; dry skin cannot absorb oxygen.

questions.q: How do frogs breathe in water and on land?
questions.a: In water through their moist skin, and on land through lungs.

questions.q: How do fish breathe?
questions.a: They gulp water; gills take in dissolved oxygen and pass it to blood, while water flows out.

questions.q: What are gills and why can they not work in air?
questions.a: Gill filaments take oxygen from water; in air they stick together and dry, so they fail.

questions.q: Why is less oxygen available to water animals?
questions.a: Water holds dissolved oxygen only (about 1%), far less than air's 21%.

concepts.title: Respiration in Plant Organs and Roots

questions.q: How do plant roots breathe?
questions.a: Root hair cells take oxygen from air spaces in soil, and release CO2 back.

questions.q: Why does waterlogged soil harm plants?
questions.a: Flooded soil has little air, so roots cannot get oxygen and may rot.

questions.q: Do plants respire through leaves? How?
questions.a: Yes - gases pass through stomata of leaves for respiration day and night.
